summary: Zhang(1) Gang [252] Jinshi # 1. His father made him responsible for the family business (jiawu), which he managed during the day. In the evening, he studied and graduated # 1 in each step of the degree process (university degree #1, jinshi in 1115). His wife was the only daughter of Li(2) Chaozheng's [975] father, Ye [3545]. All six of Gang's daughters were married to literati lineages (shizu). His ancestors are traced to those of the Fanyang Zhang by quoting the first lines of the XTS genealogy of the Zhang. The author of Gang's xingzhuang then identifies a Zhang(1) Xian(5) [13767], who held office in Zhenjiang and moved from Heshuo (i.e. Fanyang) to Zhenjiang and then a Zhang(1) Lian [13768] (and others), who all served in the administration of Southern Tang. I am arbitrarily dating the move of Xian(5) as 800 and the active year of Lian as 930. Gang's father, Ao [13775], was the first office-holder after three generations of yinju. Gang's grandson, Fu [3140], received the jinshi in 1178, was Guangxi tiju and subsequently yunpan between 1192 and 1195, was appointed Duzhi langzhong, Huaixi zongling in 1196, and was a member of the state council for a short period in 1201. Zhi Zhenjiang, 18.9a; Jingkou qi jiuzhuan, 7.14 ff; Zhang Gang, WJ, 40.1a; Liangchao beiyao, 4.28b; Lou Yue, WJ,36.17a, 41.22a. CBD, 3, 2308-9.

Shen(2) Gou [1449] Fu's [7324] son, Zhou's [7323] nephew, Liao's [1453] brother, Gua's [1450] and Pei's [1456] cousin. Placed #1 on the jinshi examination, but was made #2 because he already held office, having used his grandfather's yin to enter the service. He once lived in Suzhou. He is listed as a Hezhou jinshi in Anhui TZ, 154.7b under his zi, Wentong, which establishes a probable link with Shen(2) Li's [1452] lineage. Sima(1) Chi [1486] None of his direct patrilineal ancestors of the previous three generations held office. His cousin, Yi [3746], whose wife was from the same village (li), did not hold office. His cousin, Hao [3744], also did not hold office. The family all lived together as a large extended kinship unit in Liangshui xiang of Shanzhou, Xiaxian. Chi seems to have been the first member of the family in many generations to gain the jinshi and hold office. Previously, the lineage supported themselves through agriculture and never engaged in commerce. Guang's [1488] and Dan's [3748] father, Hong's [7063] and Kang's [7337] grandfather, Zhuo's [1487] great great grandfather. Dan's grandson, Pu [3747], was offered a post in the Jin government, but he refused. Pu's maternal grandfather was Fan(2) Chunren [559]. Fan Zuyu, WJ, 41.11a; Sima Guang, WJ, 75.10a, 79.4b; XCB, 107.12a, 122.10b; LPJ, 14.6a; SS, 298.5a-9a. CBD, 1, 436-7.少喪父，家貲數十萬，悉推諸父。舉進士。當試殿廷，忽報母亡，友匿其書，池心動，行至宮門，徘徊不能入，友告以母病，遂號慟而歸。

Jiang(1) Xiufu [10170] According to Ouyang Xiu, the family lived in Chenliu since Han. This is not listed as a Jiang(1) choronym, but, in fact, descedants of the Chenliu Jiang moved to Jiyang, whoch is a chrononym, in the Western-Eastern Jin transition. Therefore, Chenliu is the more ancient chroronym for the Jiyang Jiang (See Zhou Jiayou, 2.257).  The ancient address is Chenliu jun, Yuxian, which is Song Yongqiu xian and modern Qixian(c). Again proof that these genealogies are not fabricated since there was an easily identifiable Chenliu Jiang during the Western Jin, who could have been identified as an ancestor. Moreover, the Marquis of Liaoyang (presently Liaoxian in Shanxi, in territory of the state of Zhao during Warring states and established as a county (xian) in Western Jin and abolished in Northern Qi) cannot be identified in any standard historical source by either title or mingzi. Xiufu earned the jinshi in Tiansheng zhong, which I take as the middle sitting of the Tiansheng period or 1027. Ouyang Xiu, WJ, 33.6a-7b. CBD, 1, 533-4.

趙藩：傳　張瑩《香雪館遺詩》卷首

《宋故贈大理寺丞蔡公墓志銘幷序》：“公以天禧二年四月十八日終於章紀之里笰，享年四十七。夫人後公而終，享年四十七。女未笄而卒。奕、禀、亶、交，用文忠公蔭，俱有官：奕爲乾寧軍乾寧縣主簿，後公十年卒。禀力學，鎖中進士，官歷監察御史，公以子貴，贈大理寺丞，夫人贈滎陽縣太君，禀後公二十年卒。”據考證，蔡稟卒于慶曆五年，距其父蔡元卿去世已有27年，因此蔡元卿墓志銘中所謂“稟後公二十年卒”是一個約數，則推斷蔡奕卒年“後公十年”也應為約數，並非確切時間。
